espn-604005.headline: England have beaten New Zealand twice running once
beats: New Zealand arrive from Cardiff, where Wales beat them 35–28 for the first time in 73 years. England beat them 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. The last and only time the All Blacks lost twice in succession to England was 2002-03, and a World Cup was looming then too.

England have won four straight and put 123 points on Japan and Australia this month. Will Joseph scored five tries against Japan on his second cap and is set to keep his place. Furbank, Chessum and Atkinson are back from injury.
Dave Rennie admitted his side let their country down in Wales and promised "more edge". A win by 16 or more lifts England to third in the world and drops New Zealand to fifth.
Only one side in London wants 2002-03 repeated.

espn-604006.headline: Scotland are six men down. Japan just conceded 78
beats: Captain Sione Tuipulotu, scrum-half Ben White and number eight Jack Dempsey are among six players sent back to their clubs injured. Gregor Townsend was already planning changes to rehearse scenarios for next year's World Cup. The injuries have saved him some of the planning.

Japan come in on three straight defeats, the last a 78–15 hiding by England a week after Wales edged them 28–21. Scotland beat Australia 15–12 in the wet, a game Townsend rated one of his side's best defensive performances in recent years. Rory Darge, who led them that day, is the obvious steadying hand.

Grant Gilchrist is among the call-ups. When Japan last came to Murrayfield, in 2021, he was in support for a Scotland try in a 29–20 win that leaned on four converted tries against Rikiya Matsuda's boot.
Even a draw lifts Japan above Italy, who are Scotland's next opponents in February.

espn-604007.headline: The Springbok team sheet is a first draft
beats: In Paris, Rassie Erasmus moved his three reserve front-rowers into the starting side shortly before kick-off, reversed it 37 minutes in, and lost 21–19. He has named Malcolm Marx, Ox Nche and Wilco Louw to start in Dublin and hinted he could change again depending on Ireland's team.

Simon Easterby's view arrived with a hedge built in: "I'm not saying it's not in the spirit of the game, but maybe it's not in the spirit of the game". Erasmus has meanwhile been suspended for six matches after questioning officials, and SA Rugby has asked for a full misconduct hearing.

South Africa sit a point behind New Zealand in the South and will know what New Zealand have left them before they run out. Ireland lost here 13–24 on 22 November 2025. They need a win by 16 or more to go second in the world and push South Africa to third.
Ireland have until kick-off to learn who they are scrummaging against.

espn-604008.headline: Ten losses between them, and one side has to stop
beats: Italy and Fiji have played ten Nations Championship games between them and lost all ten. Their points differences are three apart: minus 158 for Italy, minus 161 for Fiji.

Fiji let in 54 against France and 43 against Ireland on successive weekends. Italy lost 66–7 to South Africa, then had a strong first half hour against Argentina in Genoa and still lost 19–14, with too many chances left out on the field.
Italy's breakdown coach German Fernandez says the side creates plenty but lacks the finish, and that Fiji love to play in chaos. Win, and Italy go above Fiji into 10th in the world.
Lorenzo Pani is back in the squad after a long injury. One of these sides leaves Udine with its first win of the tournament. The other lost to the only team that had none either.

espn-604009.headline: France top the North by a point; Argentina scraped Italy
beats: France go into the last pool round first in the North, and first in the North plays the Grand final. England are one point behind, so anything less than a win at Stade de France leaves the door open.

France beat South Africa 21–19 eight days ago, with Antoine Dupont, who turned 30 two days later, credited with a "masterclass". Rassie Erasmus praised French dominance at the final whistle and three days later was asking whether the refereeing amounted to manipulation.
Argentina won 19–14 in Genoa. They conceded 16 penalties and spent seven minutes with thirteen men after yellow cards to Sclavi and Elias. A week earlier Ireland put 42 past them.

Matthieu Jalibert will run the French game after tearing his right quadriceps on 20 September and breaking down again in mid-October. Lose by 16 or more and France drop to fifth in the world, behind England, the side chasing them for the final.

espn-604010.headline: Wales ended a 73-year wait. This one dates from 2021
beats: Wales beat New Zealand 35–28 on 14 November, a first win over them since 1953. Against Australia they have won just one of the past five meetings, and they are without a win over them in Cardiff since 2021.

Australia arrive on four straight defeats. New Zealand put 50 and 43 past them in October; Wales held the same side to 28. The latest loss was 15–12 at Scotland, which by recent standards counts as close.

Steve Tandy is still weighing changes despite the New Zealand result. Win by 16 or more and Wales go above Australia into eighth in the world, from a side that has sat between ninth and twelfth since July.
Victory would also give Wales only their second clean sweep of autumn internationals. In July they lost 43–0 to South Africa without scoring a try. Autumn has been kinder.

espn-604011.headline: No win yet, and the 11th-place final already booked
beats: Fourteen points behind Wales with one pool round left, Italy cannot climb out of sixth in the North. Whatever happens against Fiji in Udine on 21 November, their year ends at Allianz Stadium in the 11th-place final.
The opponent will be whoever finishes sixth in the South. Fiji sit there on no points, five behind Japan, so Italy may well see the same side twice in two matches.

Italy have lost six straight and conceded 66 to South Africa and 57 to Australia. The narrowest was the most recent: 14–19 to Argentina in Genoa, a game in which Argentina took two yellow cards and played with 13.

Breakdown coach German Fernandez says the side creates plenty and lacks only the finish, and that the players have "tutta la qualità per segnare". After London the next fixture is Scotland away in February, which leaves one game to show it.
